# Codex Remote

> A macOS menu bar app that turns a cloud account into remote Codex and Claude Code machines. You give it a provider token; it creates the server with OpenTofu, installs the agents, and wires each one up the way it expects to be reached. Open source, MIT, not affiliated with OpenAI or Anthropic.

The two agents are reached in opposite directions, which is most of why this exists. The Codex desktop app SSHes **out** to a machine and starts `codex app-server` there, so the machine has to appear in `~/.ssh/config` as a concrete host. Claude Code dials **out** from the machine to Anthropic and turns up in the user's account, so the machine needs a signed-in `claude remote-control` daemon instead. Codex Remote sets up whichever the user asked for and keeps both working across reboots.

Machines are real servers on the user's own cloud account, billed to them from the moment they exist. Nothing here is free.

## For agents

Codex Remote ships an MCP server, so an agent can create and manage machines directly. Start it with `codex-remote mcp-server` (stdio, JSON-RPC 2.0). The user adds it to their agent's MCP config once; after that the tools below are available.

Read these before acting:

- **Creating a machine spends the user's money.** `create_machine` bills to their cloud account until it is destroyed. Call `list_sizes` first and tell the user the monthly price in their own currency before you create anything.
- **Destroying is irreversible.** `destroy_machine` takes a `confirm` argument that must equal the machine's exact name — a guard against a mistyped or hallucinated one. Ask the user in their own words first.
- **`run_command` runs as root with no sandbox.** Treat it as you would a root shell on a production box.
- **Removing a machine deletes its server** when Codex Remote created it. A host the user adopted is never deleted.
- Tools are grouped into read, write and destroy permissions. A user can disable write and destroy entirely; if a call comes back refused, say so rather than working around it.

### Tools

| Tool | Level | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `list_machines` | read | Every machine, with provider, region, size, health, running agent sessions, CPU and memory |
| `machine_status` | read | Everything about one machine, including its SSH alias and workspace path |
| `list_providers` | read | Which clouds are supported and which have an account configured |
| `list_sizes` | read | Regions, sizes and images for one account, with monthly prices. Pass the region you intend to use — on EC2 image ids are per-region |
| `list_local_projects` | read | Projects the user already works on, read from Codex's and Claude Code's own records |
| `create_machine` | write | Create a server and install the agents. **Costs money** |
| `sync_project` | write | Put a local project on a machine — clones from its git remote when the work is pushed, copies it when it is not |
| `run_command` | write | Run a shell command over SSH. Root, no sandbox |
| `set_power` | write | Stop or start a machine. Stopped keeps the disk, costs less, and everything comes back on boot |
| `repair_machine` | write | Re-run the remote setup. Safe to repeat |
| `destroy_machine` | destroy | Permanently delete a machine and its server |

### A good first exchange

The user says "put Claude on a box in London". A reasonable sequence is `list_providers` to see what they have configured, `list_sizes` with the region they want, then tell them what it will cost and wait for a yes before `create_machine`. Poll `machine_status` until its stage is Ready. `sync_project` if they want their code on it.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/PandelisZ/codex-remote#readme): what it is, install, and the CLI
- [Architecture](https://codexremote.io/docs/architecture.md): how provisioning, tunnels and state fit together
- [Agents](https://codexremote.io/docs/agents.md): how Codex and Claude Code differ, and why each is wired the way it is
- [MCP](https://codexremote.io/docs/mcp.md): the MCP server, its tools and permissions
- [Projects](https://codexremote.io/docs/projects.md): project sync, git and secrets
- [Registry](https://codexremote.io/docs/registry.md): the provider registry format, for adding clouds without a release
- [Adding a provider](https://codexremote.io/docs/adding-a-provider.md): a cloud is a TofuModule plus one registry line
- [Releasing](https://codexremote.io/docs/releasing.md): signing, notarisation and the update feed
- [Design](https://codexremote.io/docs/design.md): the interface rules the app follows

## Install

```
brew install --cask pandelisz/tap/codex-remote
```

macOS 15 or later, Apple silicon or Intel. Signed with a Developer ID certificate and notarised, so a download opens normally. It lives in the menu bar and has no Dock icon.

- [Latest release](https://github.com/PandelisZ/codex-remote/releases/latest)
- [Update feed](https://codexremote.io/latest.json): version, url, sha256 — what installed copies poll
- [Provider registry](https://codexremote.io/registry.json): the default catalogue of clouds

## Clouds

Hetzner, Amazon EC2, DigitalOcean, Linode, Vultr and Scaleway, plus an existing Linux host over SSH. Every one is described as data — a provider address, some HCL, and a list of credential fields — so a cloud can be added through the registry without shipping a new build.
